commitResults.messageBody:
Java changes need a consistent project-specific style reference.

Add a reusable skill based on the SE-EDU Java conventions. Mandate
it in AGENTS.md so future Java work follows the same rules.

Commit and branch conventions need an enforceable project reference.

Add a reusable skill based on the SE-EDU Git conventions. Mandate it
in AGENTS.md so future Git work uses consistent messages and names.

The standards commits replace the repository's existing agent context.
That context defines the student profile, Java version, and Git safety
rules needed for future work.

Restore the existing instructions and append the new mandatory skill
rules so both sets of project guidance remain available.

Console interactions need repeatable checks that preserve exact input
and output for review.

Add a project skill and test plan that run cases in order, compare
output exactly, and stop at the first failure. Report both expected
and actual results so failures can be diagnosed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require UI tests after code changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Code updates can make the recorded console expectations stale. Without a
mandatory test step, output regressions may go unnoticed.

Require agents to review the UI test plan after every code update and
run the test-ui skill. Report blockers and failures instead of claiming
a successful test session.

The UI test plan covers only untyped task input, so it cannot detect
regressions in the new task commands and display formats.

Update the plan to exercise todos, deadlines, events, and completion
status changes. Include flexible deadline text and event time ranges.

commitResults.messageTitle: Minor changes to print statements. Updated ui-test-plan

commitResults.messageBody:
Isa.main handles startup, command routing, parsing, task mutation, and
output in one long method. This makes the control flow difficult to scan
and increases the risk of unrelated command changes interfering.

Extract the run loop and focused command handlers while keeping the
existing UI behavior unchanged. Name command delimiters so parsing no
longer depends on unexplained numeric offsets. This gives each method one
level of abstraction and makes future command changes more localized.

Deadline and event times use names such as by, from, and to. These names
mirror command syntax but do not explain the values when read in task
construction and formatting code.

Rename the values to dueDate, startTime, and endTime across parsing and
task models. Preserve the user-facing labels so behavior remains
unchanged, and document the updated public task APIs.

Isa handles command interaction while also owning array storage, task
counting, and indexed access. This mixes controller logic with collection
details and makes readers track two responsibilities at once.

Introduce TaskList to encapsulate fixed-capacity storage and access. Have
Isa use its add, get, and size operations while preserving all command
behavior and console output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI tests for invalid todo and unknown commands

commitResults.messageBody:
The task list only exists in memory, so changes are lost when the
application exits.

Add file-backed storage that serializes each task type and rewrites the
data file after add, mark, and unmark operations. Ignore generated user
data and extend UI coverage to ensure persistence does not alter console
output.

Saved task data is written successfully but is not restored when Isa
starts, so persistence is incomplete.

Load valid task records at startup and preserve completion states. Skip
malformed records with specific warnings, handle missing and inaccessible
data safely, and escape special field characters. Isolate UI test data so
persistence cases remain deterministic.

Deleting a task updates only the in-memory list, so the removed task
reappears after Isa restarts.

Persist the task list immediately after a successful removal and add a UI
regression case that verifies the remaining saved task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract common console interactions into Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
Isa reads commands and prints shared console messages while also
coordinating task operations. Move the greeting, dividers, command input,
errors, and farewell into Ui so one class owns these common interactions.

Keep command dispatch and task-specific responses in Isa for this small
step. Preserve the existing output and command behavior.

Isa still formats task lists, acknowledgments, and storage warnings,
which mixes console presentation with command coordination. Move those
messages into Ui so changes to response text have one home.

Keep task mutation and persistence in Isa. Preserve the existing output
and command behavior while narrowing its responsibility.

Isa identifies command words while coordinating their effects. Move
recognition into a Parser so command syntax has one place to evolve.

Keep argument extraction and task operations in Isa for a focused
increment. Preserve the existing command matching rules and responses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task argument parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
Isa still extracts descriptions, dates, and task numbers after Parser
identifies each command. Move that interpretation into Parser so Isa can
focus on task changes, persistence, and coordinating responses.

Preserve the existing command formats and validation messages in this
extraction. Keep the remaining task operations in Isa.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract exit behavior into a Command
commitResults.messageBody:
Isa directly handles the farewell and exit decision while other
commands remain in its dispatcher. Introduce an abstract Command and an
ExitCommand so the exit path establishes the execution contract for
future command extractions.

Keep the remaining command paths intact in this small step and preserve
the existing farewell output.

Isa still displays the task list directly while exit uses the new
Command contract. Move list display into ListCommand to establish a
non-exit implementation of that contract.

Keep the task list and all other command paths unchanged so this step
preserves the existing list output.

Isa constructs ExitCommand and ListCommand after Parser identifies their
types. Move that construction to Parser so Isa only coordinates their
execution and exit status.

Keep the remaining command paths in the existing dispatcher until they
have command classes of their own.

Isa still adds and saves todos directly after parsing them. Add an
AddCommand that owns the mutation, save warning, and confirmation for a
parsed task, and have Parser construct it for todo input.

Leave deadlines and events on their existing path until the same command
can handle those task types in a later increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use AddCommand for deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Isa still adds deadlines and events through a separate helper even
though todos use AddCommand. Route all three task types through the same
command and remove the duplicate add path from Isa.

Keep their existing parsing, save warning, and confirmation behavior.

Isa still validates the selected task, removes it, saves the list, and
shows the deletion response. Move those effects into DeleteCommand and
let Parser provide the requested index.

Keep missing and malformed number errors in Parser and preserve the
out-of-range error when the command executes against the task list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task status changes into MarkCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
Isa still marks and unmarks tasks, saves the list, and formats the
responses. Move both status changes into one MarkCommand and let Parser
construct it with the requested state.

Every recognized command now has a Command implementation, so simplify
Isa to execute the parsed command and inspect its exit status.

Parser first identifies a command type and then constructs its command
object in a second step. Combine recognition and construction so Isa
can request one executable Command for each input.

Preserve the existing matching order, argument parsing, and error
messages while removing the temporary command type enum.

commitResults.messageTitle: Run parsed commands directly in Isa
commitResults.messageBody:
Isa wraps command execution in a helper and handles exit with a special
break path. Run the parsed Command in the main loop, use isExit for loop
control, and print the response divider in finally.

Keep greeting, task loading, and the existing console output order while
matching the intended command-based application flow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store deadline due dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines hold arbitrary date text, so Isa cannot validate calendar dates
or display them consistently. Parse ISO dates for new deadlines, keep
them as LocalDate, and format them for display while saving ISO values.

Skip old text dates with a loading warning and update UI cases for valid,
invalid, and legacy saved dates. The UI runner cannot start Java in this
environment, so these behavior changes still need runtime verification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add date lookup and validate event times
commitResults.messageBody:
Events hold arbitrary time text, so invalid ranges cannot be detected or
searched by date. Store event endpoints as LocalDateTime, validate their
order, and add an on-date command for deadlines and spanning events.

Report malformed user input and warn when loading old or invalid saved
event records. Update UI cases for the new ISO timestamp format and date
lookup. The runner still cannot start Java in this environment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot locate tasks by a keyword without scanning the whole list.
Add FindCommand and a TaskList query that matches descriptions without
case sensitivity while keeping original task numbers in the results.

Report missing keywords and empty results, and record UI cases showing
that searches do not match date fields or change the task list. The UI
runner still cannot start Java in this environment.

Event output shows 24-hour times such as 14:00 even though users expect
2pm. Format whole hours as 2pm and times with minutes as 2:30pm while
keeping the parsed and saved ISO timestamps unchanged.

Update UI expectations for whole-hour, minute, overnight, and loaded
events. The UI runner still cannot start Java in this environment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document public APIs and task loading
commitResults.messageBody:
Task and command classes contain public methods without Javadoc,
making their responsibilities and display formats harder to follow.
Add concise method and class documentation across the task manager,
including the loading helper, without changing behavior.

The date cases cover one valid leap day but do not check that an
invalid leap day leaves the task list intact. Add a console session
that checks both outcomes together.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test phrase searches with original task numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
Search tests cover a single-word query but not a phrase inside a
description. Add a console case for case-insensitive phrase matching
and check that find does not renumber or change the task list.

Event parsing and construction can reject malformed or reversed time
ranges. Document the exceptions so callers understand the accepted
input and range constraints.
Test leap-day deadline handling
Test phrase searches with original task numbers
Document event time validation exceptions

The docs entry page is a Duke template and does not explain how to use
Isa. Replace it with concise instructions for setup, commands, task
numbering, and saved data so readers can use the current features
from GitHub Pages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Publish guide at GitHub Pages root
commitResults.messageBody:
The Pages build renders the guide as README.html, leaving no index file
at the site root and causing a 404. Set its output permalink to
index.html so the user guide opens at the published URL.
